title: Service energy and cost accounting metadata standard
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This page defines the company-wide standard for per-request energy and cost accounting metadata. The goal is to provide a consistent, compact envelope that services and proxies attach to requests and emitted telemetry so downstream billing, cost-optimization, SLO reconciliation, and sustainability metrics can reliably attribute spend and estimated energy consumption to tenants, models, and workload features.

Why this standard matters

- Unifies cost attribution across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Enables low-latency routing decisions using cost hints without leaking raw pricing data.
- Provides the data foundation for chargeback, forecast, and energy-conscious routing features.
- Supports audits and compliance with per-tenant retention and redaction policies.

Goals and constraints

1. Keep the per-request envelope small (<= 2KB) to avoid adding significant network or serialization overhead.
2. Include stable, well-documented keys (snake_case) rather than free-form tags.
3. Ensure values are typed and bounded (e.g., currency amounts in micro-units, power in millijoules).
4. Make the envelope forward-compatible: allow vendor-specific extensions under a reserved prefix.
5. Avoid embedding per-token usage details in the envelope; use async telemetry for high-granularity events.

Scope

- Applies to: edge proxies (edge-router), inference routers (inference-router), runtime sidecars (runtime-sidecar), batch job submitters, and telemetry collectors.
- Does not mandate billing rates or conversion tables — those live in the billing service and are referenced by id.
- Includes both real-time headers for short-lived routing decisions and persisted JSON envelopes for telemetry records.

Metadata fields (canonical envelope)

Use the following canonical keys in the JSON envelope attached to telemetry events and the corresponding HTTP headers for routing. Types and example values are provided. Services must include the required fields; others are optional.

| Field | Required | Type | Description | Example |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| request_id | yes | string | Global request UUID (trace-friendly). | "req_123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000" |
| tenant_id | yes | string | Tenant (customer) identifier used for billing. | "acme-corp" |
| model_id | yes | string | Canonical model identifier (catalog/model-hash). | "redwood/gptx-7b:2025-03-01" |
| estimated_energy_mJ | no | integer | Estimated energy consumed by request in millijoules (best-effort). | "4120" |
| compute_microdollars | no | integer | Estimated compute cost in micro-dollars (USD * 1e6). | "125000" |
| cost_version | yes | string | Version of the cost-accounting envelope schema (v1, v2...). | "v1" |
| pricing_ref_id | no | string | Billing service reference to the pricing table used (opaque id). | "price-table-prod-2025-03" |
| priority_class | no | string | One of: realtime, interactive, batch, bulk. Used for routing decisions. | "interactive" |
| cache_hit | no | boolean | True if the request was served from a cache (impacts cost). | "true" |
| gpu_tier | no | string | GPU tier hint (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-80gb). | "a100-80gb" |
| inference_tokens | no | integer | Optional token estimate used for cost modeling (approx). | "120" |
| appended_by | yes | string | Service that appended/last-modified this envelope (service-name). | "inference-router" |
| routed_region | no | string | Region code used for routing (e.g., us-west1). | "us-west1" |

Header mapping for real-time routing

- For low-latency routing, services must propagate a minimal header: X-RW-COST (base64-encoded JSON) or the following individual headers when size is small: X-RW-REQ-ID, X-RW-TENANT, X-RW-MODEL, X-RW-PRIORITY.
- Runtime proxies should never include sensitive pricing_ref_id in headers forwarded to external/private deployments; use internal-only header flags.

Telemetry propagation and mutation rules

1. The first ingress service (edge-router or API-gateway) must create request_id and populate tenant_id and model_id.
2. Each service that materially changes estimated_energy_mJ or compute_microdollars must append itself to appended_by and set a local delta_{field} (telemetry only). Delta fields MUST NOT be included in routing headers.
3. Runtime-sidecars may update compute_microdollars after final token count; they must emit a separate telemetry record with final accounting and mark the envelope as finalized: "cost_finalized": "true".
4. If a proxy cannot compute estimated_energy_mJ, it must omit the field (do not set 0).

Schema versioning and compatibility

- Use the cost_version field to determine compatibility. Consumers must ignore unknown fields.
- When changing types or semantics, increment cost_version and publish a migration plan in this directory.

SLOs and accuracy expectations

- Energy estimate accuracy: median absolute error <= 20% for production real-time estimates vs finalized telemetry for 95% of requests over a rolling 7-day window.
- Cost estimate accuracy: median absolute error <= 10% for compute_microdollars vs billing-service reconciliation for 99% of requests within 24 hours.
- Envelope propagation SLA: 99.9% of in-flight requests must carry either the minimal header set or the base64 envelope between edge and runtime-sidecar.

Storage, retention and redaction

- Telemetry envelopes stored in observability must omit tenant_id for analytics buckets labelled "public-aggregate". Use hashed_tenant_id when sending to cross-team aggregate pipelines.
- Raw envelopes with tenant_id and pricing_ref_id are PII-adjacent; retention default is 90 days unless tenant contract requires longer retention.
- For privacy-sensitive tenants, support redaction at ingress: redact_fields=["pricing_ref_id","estimated_energy_mJ"].

Rollout plan (recommended)

1. Week 0: Publish spec and unit tests in infra-standards repository.
2. Week 2: Edge-router and API-gateway add generation of minimal headers (X-RW-REQ-ID, X-RW-TENANT, X-RW-MODEL, X-RW-COST-VERSION). Run compatibility tests.
3. Week 4: Runtime-sidecar and inference-router adopt envelope mutation rules and emit finalized telemetry.
4. Week 6: Billing-service subscribe to finalized telemetry and run reconciliation job; measure accuracy metrics.
5. Week 8: Enable opt-in energy-based routing experiments for a small percentage of traffic (5%).

Validation and testing

- Unit test: schema validator that rejects envelopes with wrong types or missing required fields.
- Integration test: synthetic workload where compute_microdollars from runtime matches the billing-service computed microdollars within <10%.
- Smoke test: request roundtrip through edge -> runtime -> telemetry collector must include X-RW-REQ-ID and the envelope in the final event.

Example envelopes

Minimal header-encoded JSON (for routing):

X-RW-COST: eyAicmVxdWVzdF9pZCI6ICJyZXFfMTIzZSIsICJ0ZW5hbnRfaWQiOiAiYWNtZSIsICJtb2RlbF9pZCI6ICJyZWR3b29kL2dwdHgtN2I6MjAyNS0wMy0wMSIsICJjb3N0X3ZlcnNpb24iOiAidjEiIH0=

Example telemetry JSON envelope (persisted):

{
  "request_id": "req_123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp",
  "model_id": "redwood/gptx-7b:2025-03-01",
  "estimated_energy_mJ": "4120",
  "compute_microdollars": "125000",
  "cost_version": "v1",
  "pricing_ref_id": "price-table-prod-2025-03",
  "priority_class": "interactive",
  "appended_by": "runtime-sidecar",
  "routed_region": "us-west1",
  "cost_finalized": "true"
}

Operational runbook snippets

- Problem: Missing tenant_id in envelopes for a subset of traffic.
  1. Check edge-router logs for header generation failures (service: edge-router, log key: cost-envelope-generation).
  2. Validate ingress auth middleware configuration: ensure tenant extraction rules are up-to-date.
  3. If using hashed_tenant_id fallback, compare counts in realtime partition to determine scope.

- Problem: compute_microdollars differs from billing-service by > 20% (daily reconcile).
  1. Pull a sample of requests with request_id and compare runtime token counts vs billing charge pipeline.
  2. Verify pricing_ref_id mapping in billing-service and whether a new price-table was rolled without incrementing pricing_ref_id.
  3. Temporarily mark the envelope as "cost_override_reason": "investigation" in telemetry for debugging.

Governance and ownership

- Spec owner: eng-infra standards lead (Aisha Kapoor).
- Implementation owners: edge-router (team: eng-platform), inference-router (team: eng-serving-runtime), runtime-sidecar (team: eng-private-deployments).
- Review cadence: Quarterly review or when cost_version increments.

Backwards compatibility guidance

- Producer-first approach: when introducing new fields, producers may emit them flagged as optional. Consumers must tolerate absent fields.
- Deprecation: announce deprecation of a key at least 8 weeks prior and publish a migration playbook.

Open questions and future work

- Explore integrating energy models that use hardware telemetry (PState/PMU) for improved estimated_energy_mJ accuracy.
- Determine canonical hashed_tenant_id algorithm for cross-tenant analytics with privacy guarantees.
- Add support for multi-currency micro-units and per-region pricing overrides.

References

- Related playbook: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards/resource-tagging-and-request-attribution-playbook-2024
- Metrics taxonomy: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/granular-metrics-taxonomy-and-dimension-catalog-2026

Appendix: CLI validator example

# Validate an envelope file
cat envelope.json | python -m rw_cost_validator --schema v1 --check-types

Exit codes:
- 0: valid
- 1: schema error
- 2: missing required field

If you have questions or need exceptions for a specific private deployment, open a request in #eng-infra-standards and tag the spec owner.
